thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: paging rate > 250/s across gpu-pool-a (hosts 34..41). Trigger: kv-cache resident set dropped >30% (auto-alert).

maya (oncall): seeing big increase in p99 gen latency too. Customers reporting timeouts. Investigating.

arthur: I’m on metrics — p95 tokens/service is up 2.7x since 09:12 UTC. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/g/kv-cache/overview panel shows prefetch writes spiking.

jess: paging alerts + swap activity -> OOM risk. Which deploys touched continous-batching or prefetch last 24h?

eli: rollouts: PR #8912 changed default packer.max_batch_wait_ms from 12->50 for throughput test. That touched continuous-batching behavior and prefetch sweep timing.

maya (oncall): ok that sounds like a regression vector. If longer wait means bigger dynamic batches, that will push kv cache churn and prefetch storms. Lower priority short requests get starved.

arthur: confirmed trace sampling: mixed short/long workload queueing increased median batch size x3 on host GPU-36. Short requests backed up behind long ones -> high tail latency.

incident-bot: CUSTOMER IMPACT: 7 hosted customers affected, visible as failed responses (HTTP 504) and token generation >15s.

jess: tagging severity-2 for now. Escalate to eng-runtime and oncall.

maya (oncall): @sre-oncall can you assist with live mitigation? We need to reduce paging ASAP and restore short-request SLO.

sre-oncall: joining. Priorities: 1) stop kv-cache blowup (reduce prefetch) 2) limit batch growth for mixed shapes 3) stabilize hosts (swap/oom).

eli: quick config rollback option: revert packer.default_wait to 12ms cluster-wide. That avoids new batching behaviour. I can push a runtime config hotfix to the control plane.

arthur: also we can apply a short-request priority rule in batch-scheduler: enable preempt_short_requests: true for the in-prod route group. Pretty minimal change.

maya (oncall): do both. Hotfix packer.wait rollback first, then enable priority preempt. Sequence: rollback -> monitor 5m -> apply scheduler rule -> monitor 15m.

jess: I'll open INC-4512 with timeline and customer list. Link: https://jira.redwood/inc/4512

eli: starting rollback now. Command: \n```
/rollout apply config packer.default_wait=12 --scope=prod --tag=hotfix-176912
```

incident-bot: DEPLOY: rollback hotfix-176912 started by eli.

arthur: seeing batch size drop on gpu-36 within 40s. p95 latency trending down. Paging rate still elevated but falling.

sre-oncall: keep an eye on swap. If any host crosses 60% swap we need to drain.

maya (oncall): swap on gpu-38 still high 72% and kernel dropping LRU. Queue draining slower there. Prepare a drain step.

jess: prepping customer comms - short note for affected customers stating we're mitigating a batching regression, targeted fix applied, monitoring.

eli: rollback finished. Incident-bot: DEPLOY: rollback hotfix-176912 completed (success).

arthur: nice signal — p99 dropped from 12.4s -> 3.1s over the next 3m on average. Paging down to ~45/s.

maya (oncall): continue with batch-scheduler rule to protect short requests. Command to apply: \n```
/feature-toggle set batch-scheduler.preempt_short_requests=true --env=prod
```

incident-bot: FEATURE: batch-scheduler.preempt_short_requests enabled by maya (oncall).

sre-oncall: after enabling preempt, p50/p95 short-request latency back to SLO. Mixed workload fairness improved. No new swap spikes.

arthur: we still have a few hosts with higher eviction counts; starting a rolling drain of gpu-38 to reclaim memory and reduce paging. Will move traffic to spare pool.

maya (oncall): go ahead. ETA drain 6m per host.

eli: note: need a postmortem to address the packer default change landing without perf canary. We should add a gating rule in PR checks for batching-affecting flags.

jess: added follow-ups to INC-4512: add canary for batch config changes, update runbook to include immediate preempt toggle, add customer follow-up templates.

incident-bot: RUNBOOK CHECKPOINT: page_threshold cleared, mitigation applied, oncall handoff scheduled.

maya (oncall): handing off to arthur for post-incident cleanup and RCA lead. I'll be available for comms. If anything regresses re-ping on this thread.

arthur: taking handoff. Next steps: collect heap/kv metrics for 30m window, trace top 200 slow requests, correlate with commit id #8912, and run a controlled canary of packer.wait change with priority preempt enabled.

jess: customer comms sent (template). No escalations to sales yet.

sre-oncall: system stabilized. Setting incident to monitoring -> resolved in 2h if no regressions.

maya (oncall): thanks everyone. Patch/PRs to follow.

eli: PR to add gating for batching flags posted: https://git.redwood/pr/8920.

arthur: logging RCA owner + timelines in INC-4512. Closing active paging alerts.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: Severity decreased to S3 (monitoring). Logs and traces archived to /incidents/1769128000/ for 90d.

maya (oncall): end of thread for now — keep follow-up items in INC-4512. :thumbsup:
